evidence.snippet: Reticulocytopenia occurs in 20-40% of autoimmune hemolytic anemia cases and is a poor prognostic factor.

nodes.description: Investigational long-acting inhibitor of activated C1s in CAD. An early single-dose study was completed, while the subsequent repeat-dose study NCT04802057 is terminated in the current registry.

evidence.reference_title: A Multicenter, Phase 1b, Open Label, Nonrandomized, Single Dose Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability and Activity of BIVV020 in Adults With Cold Agglutinin Disease
evidence.snippet: To assess the safety and tolerability in participants with cold agglutinin disease (CAD), after a single dose of intravenous (IV) BIVV020

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemias: Challenges in Diagnosis and Therapy.
evidence.snippet: the second-generation active C1s inhibitor riliprubart (formerly SAR445088, BIVV020), characterized by a prolonged half-life and thus a longer dosing interval than that of sutimlimab

nodes.description: Investigational BTK inhibition for warm AIHA in the phase II LUMINA 2 study. Early open-label findings require confirmation; the ongoing extension does not establish an approved AIHA indication.

evidence.reference_title: A Multicenter, Open-label, Phase IIb Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety and Pharmacokinetics of Rilzabrutinib in Patients With Warm Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia (LUMINA 2)
evidence.snippet: All participants will receive rilzabrutinib orally. The screening period is up to 28 days, followed by a treatment period of 24 weeks for Part A. Participants who complete Part A and are deemed eligible for Part B can continue in the Core Part B period followed by an Extended Part B period for up to 253 weeks.

evidence.reference_title: Beneath the surface in autoimmune hemolytic anemia: pathogenetic networks, therapeutic advancements and open questions.
evidence.snippet: Rilzabrutinib, a reversible covalent BTK inhibitor, has been evaluated in a multicentric open-label phase 2b trial

nodes.description: Anti-CD20 B-cell depletion is a preferred second-line treatment for warm AIHA and may be introduced earlier in severe disease. It also targets the pathogenic B-cell clone in CAD, as monotherapy or combined with bendamustine in suitable patients; response magnitude and durability differ by subtype.

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemias: Challenges in Diagnosis and Therapy.
evidence.snippet: The anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody rituximab has become the preferred 2nd line being able to induce 70–80% of responses.

nodes.description: Clone-directed combination used in suitable CAD patients who require treatment. It can produce deeper and more durable responses than rituximab alone but adds cytotoxic and infectious risks, particularly relevant in frail patients.

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemias: Challenges in Diagnosis and Therapy.
evidence.snippet: the combination of rituximab plus bendamustine resulted in increased response rate (78%, with complete responses in 53%), and long response duration (more than 7 years)

nodes.description: Investigational SYK inhibitor evaluated in a Chinese phase II/III study. The published phase II component randomized 21 patients (16 active, five placebo) for eight weeks, followed by open-label treatment for everyone. The 24-week overall response of 14/21 (67%) therefore includes crossover and is not a maintained placebo-controlled comparison.

evidence.reference_title: Sovleplenib in patients with primary or secondary warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia: results from phase 2 of a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2/3 study.
evidence.snippet: All 21 patients completed the 0-8-week double-blind treatment and entered the open-label treatment period.

evidence.reference_title: Sovleplenib in patients with primary or secondary warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia: results from phase 2 of a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2/3 study.
evidence.snippet: The overall haemoglobin response rate was 67% (14 of 21 patients) by week 24, and durable haemoglobin response rate was 48% (ten of 21 patients) by week 24.

nodes.description: Partial macrophage removal of antibody-coated red-cell membrane produces spherocytes; this blood-film finding is not specific for AIHA.

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemias: Classifications, Pathophysiology, Diagnoses and Management.
evidence.snippet: In wAIHA, this leads to the degradation of the RBC membrane, causing transformation into spherocytes

nodes.description: A later-line option for selected fit patients with refractory warm AIHA, after accounting for lifelong infection and thrombotic risks. It is generally ineffective in CAD because complement-opsonized cells are cleared predominantly in the liver.

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemias: Challenges in Diagnosis and Therapy.
evidence.snippet: It may be considered in young low comorbid patients after vaccination against capsulated organisms, and accounting for a life-long increase in infectious and thrombotic risk.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical features and treatment of primary autoimmune hemolytic anemia in childhood.
evidence.snippet: icterus and hepatomegaly /splenomegaly was the most common physical findings

nodes.description: C1s inhibition for CAD rapidly controls complement-mediated hemolysis and improves anemia and fatigue. Continued dosing is usually needed; it does not remove the B-cell clone or directly treat agglutination-mediated acrocyanosis and Raynaud symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term efficacy and safety of continued complement C1s inhibition with sutimlimab in cold agglutinin disease: CADENZA study Part B.
evidence.snippet: Following a 9-week washout, inhibition of CP activity was reversed, and haemolytic markers approached baseline levels.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term efficacy and safety of continued complement C1s inhibition with sutimlimab in cold agglutinin disease: CADENZA study Part B.
evidence.snippet: The mechanism of action of sutimlimab means that it affects the complement-mediated symptoms of CAD, such as haemolysis, anaemia, and fatigue, rather than the cold-induced, agglutination-mediated circulatory symptoms, such as acrocyanosis and Raynaud's phenomenon.

nodes.description: Membrane attack complex formation causes intravascular hemolysis. It is prominent in PCH and can increase during CAD exacerbations; it should not replace hepatic extravascular clearance as the predominant stable-CAD mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Beneath the surface in autoimmune hemolytic anemia: pathogenetic networks, therapeutic advancements and open questions.
evidence.snippet: terminal complement activation with membrane attack complex (MAC) C5b-C9 formation is generally absent during stable clinical phases and occurs predominantly during acute exacerbations or in severe disease

nodes.description: Warm-AIHA cohorts show increased IL-17 production and a higher Th17/Treg ratio. Serum IL-17 correlates with LDH and bilirubin, but not hemoglobin or reticulocyte count; this association does not establish that IL-17 directly destroys red cells.

evidence.reference_title: Regulatory T-cell dysfunctions are associated with increase in tumor necrosis factor α in autoimmune hemolytic anemia and participate in Th17 polarization.
evidence.snippet: the serum concentration of IL-17 positively correlated with markers of RBC destruction, namely lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and bilirubin

nodes.description: Venous and arterial thrombosis can complicate AIHA, especially during active hemolysis. A tertiary-center cohort observed events in 33/287 patients (11.4%); this selected cohort is not a universal frequency estimate.

evidence.reference_title: Intravascular hemolysis and multitreatment predict thrombosis in patients with autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
evidence.snippet: Thirty-three AIHA patients (11.4%) experienced thrombosis, 70% of whom hospitalized.

nodes.description: Consider anticoagulant prophylaxis according to active hemolysis, hospitalization, additional thrombosis risks and bleeding risk. In a nonrandomized prospective subset with LDH at least 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, no thromboses occurred in 17 heparin-treated patients versus five events among 16 untreated patients. Optimal selection and duration remain uncertain.

evidence.reference_title: Intravascular hemolysis and multitreatment predict thrombosis in patients with autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
evidence.snippet: In those receiving prophylaxis no thrombotic complications occurred, whereas five thrombotic episodes were registered in the remaining 16 cases.

nodes.description: Warm-reactive IgG coats erythrocytes at physiological temperature. Antigen specificity varies; band 3 and Rh-associated reactivity should not be treated as a single universal target.

evidence.reference_title: Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemias: Classifications, Pathophysiology, Diagnoses and Management.
evidence.snippet: IgG antibodies have a strong attraction to red blood cells when the temperature is at the normal level of the human body (37 °C).

nodes.description: Investigational BTK inhibition being evaluated separately in relapsed/refractory warm AIHA and primary CAD. The two registered populations should not be pooled as established efficacy evidence.

evidence.reference_title: Beneath the surface in autoimmune hemolytic anemia: pathogenetic networks, therapeutic advancements and open questions.
evidence.snippet: zanubrutinib, a next-generation, irreversible BTK inhibitor, is under investigation in a phase 2 trial (NCT05922839) for patients with warm AIHA and in a separate phase 2 trial involving CAD (NCT06067048).
